title: Tea under glass and seven days
subtitle: In which the visit is given a deadline, Hormuz a calendar, and Notre-Dame its first pope since the fire.
lede: The ceremony is over. The deadlines remain.

body:
The visit ends before the deadline begins. In Washington the two men drink tea. Over Hormuz lies a calendar of seven days. In Paris a pope enters a cathedral raised from ash.

I. Tea under glass

What was pomp yesterday is departure today. Donald Trump and Xi Jinping close the state visit with tea at the White House and a walk through the National Archives. The Constitution and the Bill of Rights lie under glass — visible, untouchable. The trade truce now runs to 10 January. Further meetings: APEC in China, the G20 in Florida. Pandas for Atlanta. The great disputes remain where they lay yesterday. Only the calendar has moved. 1 2

II. Seven days

What is new on the water is not the fire but the deadline. Abbas Araghchi says Tehran has sent Washington, via Qatar, a seven-day plan. If the blockade, oil sanctions and frozen assets are addressed and a regional ceasefire holds, Hormuz could reopen on the sixth day. The White House speaks of constructive talks through mediators. The choice, Araghchi says, now sits with the United States. 3

In the Red Sea the deadline does not change the ammunition. The Houthis claim hits on Yanbu; Riyadh counts six intercepted missiles. Macron sends soldiers, radar and air defence to the terminal. A European flag stands in front of a Saudi tap. 4

III. In daylight

Over Kyiv the blows fall in daylight. Seven dead, among them a fourteen-year-old boy. Zelenskyy says Trump has given a final decision on Patriot licences — and asks him to use China's weight in Moscow. The dead of this afternoon do not wait on licences. 5 6

IV. The white guest in the ash

Leo XIV begins four days in France. At UNESCO he calls the United Nations a crisis of effectiveness: dialogue as farce. In the evening, vespers in rebuilt Notre-Dame — the first pope there since the fire of 2019. Outside, hundreds of thousands wait. 8

The chronicler's close

The calendar has three new dates: 10 January, seven days for Hormuz, four days for a pope. Whether a deadline is a peace will be shown only tomorrow morning.
